paper.title: FlowTransformer: A Transformer Framework for Flow-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems

scope: Table III UNSW-NB15 v2: all 8 settings across all 4 architecture families, plus Laya. Not the complete 3-dataset hyperparameter grid.

dataset.name: NF-UNSW-NB15-v2
dataset.split: First 90% train; last 10% test; source CSV order

input.features: 37 author-selected fields; no IP addresses or labels
input.target: binary attack label of final flow
input.preprocessing: Original StandardPreProcessing(32), fit on train only; unknown categorical behavior preserved; sorted numerical feature names
input.laya: CSV serialization of identical preprocessed information; numeric float32 round-trip 9 significant digits; categorical codes inverted to train mapping values; no truncation; max 8192 tokens

training.stop_implementation: upstream: six epochs without a new minimum individual batch loss (stale > 5)
training.sampling: 50% attack, 50% benign; random target rows, contiguous windows; identical pregenerated schedules
training.checkpoint_selection: last epoch reached by training-loss stopping; no test-selected checkpoint

evaluation.epochs: after epoch 7 and final epoch as upstream; final is primary
evaluation.aggregation: all three repeats plus mean, standard deviation and best repeat; best repeat is descriptive paper convention, not deployment selection
evaluation.timing: same GPU after training, warm state; 50 random batches x 4 repetitions; median per batch then mean; additional batch-1 p50/p95, serialization-inclusive latency

differences_and_unreported_details: Paper says 90/10; code example uses UNSW 97.5/2.5. Paper text governs; published Table III values not directly comparable cohorts.
Winning per-setting learning rates absent. Fixed author-example Adam 0.001 for scratch models and conservative pretrained Laya 1e-5 from paper rate grid; no claim of optimal tuning.
64 steps/epoch and batch128 from public main.py, not explicitly stated in paper. An epoch is 8192 balanced draws, not a full pass through 2.15M training rows.
Record dense dimension128 for first encoder row inferred from exact published parameter count; other record dimensions64, categorical16.
Minimum3 repeats paper convention implemented as exactly3. Published best-of-grid numbers separated from fixed-setting reruns.
Python3.11/Linux and newer framework/GPU differ from paper Python3.9/Windows/RTX2070MaxQ.
Streaming batch assembly replaces full test-window materialization; architecture and upstream preprocessing unchanged.
v2 flow CSV lacks timestamps: consecutive rows are not proven chronological, host-related or multi-step attacks.
Test feature duplicates present in train are retained to match paper split, separately audited.
